newsitem.title: FINLAND: Weak dollar dents Helsinki, despite Nokia strength.
newsitem.headline: Weak dollar dents Helsinki, despite Nokia strength.

text.p: Shares edged downward in moderate trade on Thursday despite early gains as Japanese strong-yen comments hit the dollar and boosted losses in forestry and metal sector stocks, brokers said.
The HEX index slipped 0.12 percent to 2,224.47. Volume was fair at 360 million markka.

"The comments depressed the whole of Europe," one broker said referring to remarks by a Japanese official signalling that the dollar's recovery against the yen was nearly complete and Japan's economy stronger than the markets believed.

The HEX was also dragged by wholesale and retail group Kesko, which fell on Wednesday's news that the EU was not satisfied with Kesko's proposal to sell its TukoSpar unit to win approval for its merger with former rival Tuko, they said.
Bourse engine Nokia closed active trade up 4.40 markka at 220.00 in Helsinki and extended Wednesday's strong gains on early Wall Street.
Nokia accounted for almost half of total bourse volume, and brokers said the share could set the market's tone on Friday.

Merita's A share recovered from early losses and closed active trade up 0.10 markka at 13.90 after overseas investors had digested the news of the bank's January-September earnings largely in line with expectations.
Pharmaceuticals group Orion's B share fell 3.00 markka in moderate trade to end at 152.00 after the company said it did not expect to launch its breast cancer drug in the U.S. this year.
Europe's biggest forestry group UPM-Kymmene ended modest trade 0.80 markka lower at 87.00 after rebounding from a new all-time low 85.50.
Paper machine maker Valmet tracked forestries lower, losing 0.50 markka to 70.50 in lively trade.
